title: Micky van de Ven says noise around Tottenham ‘brings more trouble’
content:
Micky van de Ven has said that the noise around Tottenham Hotspur “brings more trouble”.

Spurs have not won a game in the Premier League since December and are only one point above the relegation zone ahead of Sunday’s crucial fixture against 17th-placed Nottingham Forest. Head coach Thomas Frank was sacked in February and replaced by Igor Tudor on an interim basis until the end of the season.

Tudor lost his opening four games in charge including last week’s humiliating 5-2 defeat to Atletico Madrid in the first leg of their Champions League round-of-16 tie. Spurs lost six games in a row for the first time in their 144-year history but broke the sequence with a 1-1 draw against Liverpool last weekend. Van de Ven missed the game at Anfield through suspension after being sent off in the 3-1 defeat to Crystal Palace earlier this month.

Last week, The Athletic reported that some first-team players who are determined to arrest Spurs’ decline have expressed displeasure at the application of some of their team-mates, who they believe are not motivated to help their cause. The Athletic has even been told that one player has expressed to his team-mates he is not too concerned by the possibility of relegation because he believes he can and will leave the club this summer.

Before the return leg at home against Atletico on Wednesday, Van de Ven said the squad were feeling “frustrated” but insisted they still care.

“People are just making things up, and it’s just frustrating for us as well, because it brings so much more trouble as well, because the fans are starting to believe this,” the Netherlands international said.

“They start saying, the guys don’t care anymore what’s going to happen in the club about the situation, but trust me, all the people involved on the pitch, the staff, the players, everyone, they care so much about the situation we’re in right now. We just want to turn things around, and that’s the most important, that’s the main focus for everyone.”

Van de Ven described Tottenham’s season as “really tough for everyone at the club” and admitted he has underperformed. The centre-back revealed he apologised to his team-mates in the dressing room following his dismissal against Palace.

“For me, it’s just most important that I keep showing to everyone that I always give 100 per cent to this club. I will always do as long as I play,” he continued. “For me, the most important is that we turn things around right now.

“If people say things, then people say things. Obviously people are going to believe things that are not true. There’s nothing I can do about that.”
